On Aug. 17th through the 21st I took a week-long crash course on how to use R for Data Science.




::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(tidyverse)

ggplot(
  data = mpg, 
  mapping = aes(
    x = cty,
    y = hwy
  )
)+ geom_point()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](index_files/figure-html/MPG in city vs highway-1.png){fig-alt='Scatterplot of city versus highway fuel economy in miles per gallon for cars in the mpg dataset, showing that cars with better city mileage also get better highway mileage.' width=1400}
:::
:::


This is great, but one thing we learned about is the importance of clear labels using the `labs()` function.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(tidyverse)

ggplot(
  data = mpg, 
  mapping = aes(
    x = cty,
    y = hwy
  )
)+ geom_point() + 
  geom_smooth() + 
  labs(
    x = "City Mileage",
    y = "Highway Mileage", 
    title = "City vs Highway"
  )
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr}

```
`geom_smooth()` using method = 'loess' and formula = 'y ~ x'
```
